descriptive_title: Grade 2 Mathematics: Algebra (Modelling) — Mathematical Modelling for Real-Life Town Situations (C4)
subject: Mathematics

curriculum_expectations.C4: apply the process of mathematical modelling to represent, analyse, make predictions, and provide insight into real-life situations

unit_overview: A 5-day Grade 2 unit on mathematical modelling (C4) framed around 'Math in My Town' — Mayor Mira the Math Mayor and her assistant Town Tom. Day 1 introduces the modelling cycle for town situations: SITUATION → QUESTION → DATA → PREDICT → REFLECT. Day 2 collects town data (visitors, library books, recess minutes). Day 3 predicts town outcomes using simple rules. Day 4 reflects and refines models with real numbers. Day 5 closes with child-chosen capstone projects modelling situations from their own town life. Each lesson includes an expanded_walkthrough covering Grade-2 misconceptions in modelling.
unit_learning_goal: Children will apply the 5-step modelling cycle to a real-life town situation: pick a situation, ask a math question, collect data, predict, reflect.

lesson_arc.big_idea: Math is everywhere in our town: at the library, the park, the school, the rink. Modelling means asking math questions about real-life situations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can describe a town situation and ask a math question about it.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Mayor Mira tours the town pointing out math; children identify situations and ask questions.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We answer math questions by collecting DATA. Counts, measurements, observations.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can collect data to answer a math question about my town.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children collect data on town situations (visitors, books borrowed, recess minutes) and record on a chart.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We use rules + data to PREDICT future town outcomes. If 5 buses arrive each morning, predict 25 buses in 5 days.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can use a rule to predict a town outcome.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children use simple rules and town data to predict outcomes for the next day or week.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We check our predictions against what really happened. Sometimes the model needs refining.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can compare a prediction to actual data and refine my model.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children compare predictions to actual data; suggest refinements to make the model better.

lesson_arc.big_idea: We can model ANY town situation. Pick a topic from your life, ask a question, build a model.
lesson_arc.student_learning_goal: I can model a real-life town situation from my own life.
lesson_arc.one_line_summary: Children invent a town modelling project — situation, question, data, predict, reflect — and share.

recurring_characters.name: Mayor Mira the Math Mayor
recurring_characters.role: Lead character. A friendly mayor in a sash who shows children the math in their town. Anchors all 5 lessons.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A friendly young mayor wearing a town sash, holding a small notebook and pencil. Cheerful smile, big glasses, hat with a town badge.

recurring_characters.name: Town Tom the Town Helper
recurring_characters.role: Mayor Mira's assistant. The 'count it' character — gathers data with Mira. Cameo Lessons 2-5.
recurring_characters.visual_description: A young helper with a clipboard and tape measure, wearing a vest with town-mayor logo. Eager expression, taking notes.

assessment_strategy.diagnostic: Lesson 1 town-question snapshot: each child reads 4 town situations and writes 1 math question for each.
assessment_strategy.formative: Lesson 2 data tracker; Lesson 3 prediction tracker; Lesson 4 reflection tracker.
assessment_strategy.summative: Lesson 5 capstone — children invent a town modelling project. Captures C4 in one creative artifact.

pedagogical_notes: C4 in Grade 2 extends modelling to richer numbers and town-scale situations (counts to 100).
The 5-step modelling cycle (situation, question, data, predict, reflect) anchors every lesson.
Real Canadian town examples ground the work: bus arrivals, hockey games, public library books.
Differentiation: emerging children stay with simple counts; extending children build multi-step rules.
The 'refine' step matters even at Grade 2 — children must understand that models improve with data.
canadian_context_notes: Real-life examples: number of TTC bus stops in a route, books borrowed from the public library, kids on the playground at recess, hockey rink visitors on a Saturday.
Tim Hortons line counts at lunch; Canadian Tire customer arrivals.
Town events: weekend farmers' market, summer fair counts.
